propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same S3 ref, git ls-remote returns the ref at two SHAs and a fresh clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable.

The git-remote-s3 helper's cmd_push rejects any push while len(bundles) > 1 before writing anything, and subsequent fetches cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, causing push retries to stall indefinitely.
Upstream's git-s3 doctor is interactive-only (blocking on input() prompts) and discards non-chosen heads to orphan refs, losing unique events from the append-only log and violating data durability.

The heal must perform a lossless 2-parent merge of divergent bundle heads (iteratively, not octopus), following rebar's existing sync reconciliation semantics, ensuring every unique commit from every head is reachable in the result.

The heal must write the merged tip as a new bundle to S3 before deleting any original bundle and never delete the merged tip, guaranteeing at least one bundle carrying the full merged history remains at every crash point.

Concurrent repairs must serialize via the helper's S3 lock; a process that cannot acquire the lock must back off and converge on the winner's collapsed remote, rather than performing a second independent heal.
